subject: Detection coverage & notification protocols — misuse monitoring
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@omega-financial.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@omega-financial.com
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Detection coverage & notification protocols for Redwood deployment

Vanessa —

Thanks for taking the time so far. As we scope the security review for a potential pilot, our InfoSec team has a few focused questions about how Redwood detects and notifies on misuse patterns. We’re trying to confirm coverage and SLAs so we can map to our internal incident taxonomy. High-level asks below — can your team provide short answers and sample outputs where practical?

1) Detection surface: which signal types do you use for automated misuse classification (e.g., model output heuristics, prompt pattern matching, user and rate anomalies, embeddings similarity to banned content)? Do you run any client-side or edge checks?
2) Coverage: can you outline what percentage of customer traffic is covered by real-time detection vs batched detection and how that varies by plan (hosted vs dedicated vs private)?
3) Notification/erroring: what are the default notification channels (webhook, email, SIEM integration) and what thresholds trigger immediate triage vs batch reporting? Can you confirm your SLA for an initial triage or notice to the customer when a high-severity misuse signal is detected?
4) Evidence and audit trail: what artifacts do you include in a report (token deltas, model logits, cached KV snippets, request/response pairs, timestamps) and how long are those retained for enterprise customers?
5) Throttling/fallback: describe actions that the platform takes automatically (reject, rate-limit, downgrade model, route to safer model) and whether customers can customize these policies.

If possible, please attach a short example alert (redacted) and a one-page coverage summary. Our deadlines are tight — we’d appreciate a response by EOD Monday PST.

Appreciate it —
Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Application Security
Omega Financial

Date: Sat, 11 Sep 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Detection coverage & notification protocols for Redwood deployment

Vanessa —

Draft answers and attachments attached. Summary below and files in the thread: misuse-detection-matrix.csv (signal taxonomy + detection confidence), alerting-diagram.png (how we escalate), and a sample redacted alert payload (small JSON snippet in the CSV notes). Paste of the key points: 

1) Detection surface:
- Model-output heuristics: pattern-matchers and trained classifiers over token sequences (language-model-aware features such as repetition, hallucination markers, and policy-keyword detectors).
- Prompt-pattern matching: regex and ML-based fingerprinting against known malicious prompt templates.
- Behavioral signals: per-user rate anomalies, sudden shift in prompt embeddings, geographic and API-key velocity heuristics.
- Embedding similarity: vector compare against prohibited-content corpus (supporting fuzzy matches).
- No client-side checks are required by default for hosted; customers running Redwood Private can deploy edge filters via our SDKs.

2) Sample alert (redacted):
- Severity: HIGH
- Trigger: model-output heuristic score > 0.92 AND embedding-similarity > 0.85
- Evidence: request_id, truncated prompt (first 120 chars), generated_text hash, top-3 model logits, timestamp, matched policy tag
- Actions taken: immediate non-blocking webhook to customer + queued for human review in case of HIGH severity; optional auto-block if customer enables strict fail-open=false policy.

I kept the sample compact to avoid sending raw tokens. The CSV explains field mappings for our alert payload. If you want a slightly longer redacted sample, I can produce one but will need Security approval first.

-ben
Ben Carter
Product Security Liaison
Redwood Inference

To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@omega-financial.com>
Cc: security@omega-financial.com, ben.carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Detection coverage & notification protocols for Redwood deployment

Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. Please find consolidated answers below and three attachments: detection-coverage-summary.pdf (one-page coverage snapshot), misuse-detection-matrix.csv (signal taxonomy + sample redacted payload fields), and alerting-diagram.png (escalation flow). We’ve redacted tokens from the example alert but included the structural artifacts you requested. If you’d like a live walkthrough of the alert payload in our console, we can set up a 30-minute session next week.

Inline answers: 
1) Detection surface:
- We operate multiple orthogonal detectors: model-output heuristics (LLM-aware classifiers), prompt-template fingerprinting, embedding-similarity checks against curated prohibited corpora, and behavioral anomaly detectors (per-key velocity, geo/sudden spike detection). Customers on Redwood Private may also deploy optional client/edge filters using our SDKs; hosted customers are covered by server-side detectors.

2) Coverage:
- Hosted API: ~92% of incoming requests assessed by real-time detectors (the remainder processed through near-real-time pipelines for cost efficiency); Dedicated pools: ~96% real-time for reserved capacity configurations; Private: configurable, typically >98% if deployed with local inference routing and edge filters. These numbers are historical averages and depend on token length and burst patterns — we include coverage breakdowns in the attached PDF.

3) Notification/erroring & SLA:
- Channels: webhook (recommended), email, and SIEM integrations (Splunk/Datadog via secure forwarders).
- Immediate triage: HIGH-severity signals generate an immediate webhook + console incident and an automated email to the customer’s security contacts.
- SLA: initial triage notice within 2 hours for HIGH, 8 hours for MEDIUM, and 48 hours for LOW signals for Enterprise customers on a Dedicated or Private contract. Hosted customers have a 4-hour HIGH triage target under our standard support plan; these SLAs are contractable for Dedicated/Private deals.

4) Evidence and audit trail:
- We attach structured artifacts: request_id, truncated prompt (first 120 chars), generated response hash (no raw tokens unless customer requests and signs Data Access terms), top-k logits, matched policy tag, model-version, region, and timestamp. For enterprise contracts we retain these artifacts for up to 13 months by default; retention windows are configurable via the Console and can be extended via contract addendum.

5) Throttling/fallback actions:
- Default automated actions: soft-fail (flag + alert), hard-block (reject) if strict mode enabled, model-fallback to a safer, constrained variant, and per-key rate-limiting. Customers can configure policies per-API-key or per-route in the Console; Role-based access controls ensure only authorized admins can change enforcement levels.

Attachments: detection-coverage-summary.pdf (one-pager), misuse-detection-matrix.csv (schema + redacted structure), alerting-diagram.png (escalation diagram).

Related links: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/Omega-Detection-Examples — contains an anonymized example incident and an exportable CSV you can feed to your SIEM.

If this looks good I’ll give Security a heads-up for a brief review of the redacted sample (we shouldn’t need an on-site review). Would you like the 30-minute demo next Tue/Wed?

Best —
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0183
